alignments.note: Supplied object noun that does not carry נתן's lexeme; added under rule 44. The ASV italic corroborates without deciding, rule 7.
Substantival adjective with a supplied generic *man*, rule 31.
Subject pronoun and auxiliaries with the verb; discontinuous around *yet* under rule 25.
Bare English object leaves the preposition nothing, rule 40.

Subject pronoun and auxiliary with the verb, rule 17. לֶקַח is this Hiphil's own bare direct object, with no marker and no preposition on it, so the supplied *in* by which the English reaches it belongs to the verb's unit under rule 44's supplied-preposition clause and not to the noun under rule 33, whose third limit defers there. Head stays on the lexical verb, which rule 44 leaves unaffected. The competing reading gives *in* to the noun on the ground that another preposition would have served; that test does not separate the two cases, since an English recasting of a transitive Hebrew verb always leaves a relation to choose. Aligned as PRO.9.15 aligns the *on* of *go right on their ways*.
Bare direct object of יָסַף, keeping only its own word; the supplied *in* has gone to the verb under rule 44.

review_notes: Patched for the chapter-wide split with PRO.9.15: a preposition the ASV supplies to reach a Hebrew verb's bare direct object is the verb's under rule 44, whichever preposition it chose.
Both לְ datives before the adjectives remain unrepresented for the same reason as in PRO.9.8.
The italic *instruction* remains added: נתן's lexeme is already written by *Give*, so the supplied object noun answers to no morpheme.
